sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Unitary National Jurisdiction, no sub-tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition) with pragmatic adoption of Common Law commercial and trust-type instruments for private foundation law
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA) in force 31 October 2012
Panama–United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (signed 2019, in force 2020)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Panama Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Ley de Fundaciones de Interés Privado), as amended by Law No. 41 of 2012 and Law No. 189 of 2021, Articles 1-40; supplementary application of Executive Decree No. 10 of 1996 and the Panamanian Civil Code.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama), Dirección General, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (Foundation Charter Deed) with annexed Reglamento (Foundation Regulations)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Law 25 of 1995. The Foundation Charter must declare an initial endowment, commonly US$10,000, sufficient to fulfill the foundation's purposes. The endowment must be paid or secured by the Founder before or at execution of the deed; no government escrow account is mandated, but a bank deposit receipt is recommended as evidentiary support.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FOUNDATION COUNCIL RESOLUTION NO. 1 - RESOLVED, that the Foundation Council of [Name], acting under Panama Law No. 25 of 1995, hereby: (1) accepts the Founder's subscription and payment of the initial endowment of US$10,000.00; (2) adopts the registered office at [Street Address], Panama City, Republic of Panama, as the Foundation's legal domicile; (3) appoints [President], [Secretary], and [Treasurer] as council officers, each to serve until resignation or removal; (4) appoints [Resident Agent Firm] as Resident Agent. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute registry filings, and administer foundation assets in accordance with the Charter and Regulations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Foundation Charter and Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian attorney (abogado) engaged by the Founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct counsel to draft the Escritura de Constitución and the Reglamento. The deed must specify the foundation name (bearing 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or 'Foundation'), initial endowment, detailed foundation purposes (including ownership of Ro-Ro vessel-owning entities and participation in maritime shipping), council members, beneficiary designation mechanism, protector (if any), registered office in Panama, and the Founder's reserved powers.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Founder's passport or corporate register document
Proposed foundation name availability letter from Registro Público
Foundation purpose and beneficiary statement
Registered office address confirmation from the Resident Agent
Initial endowment payment receipt or sworn declaration of endowment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusingly similar, submit three alternative names and re-file the name availability certificate; if the deed text is incomplete, counsel issues an amendment before notarization at no additional registry step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de la República de Panamá (Panamanian Public Notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Founder (or attorney-in-fact by power of attorney) appears before the notary with the final draft deed. The notary verifies identity, certifies the execution, and issues a certified protocolized copy. All original signatures and the initial endowment payment must be evidenced before the notary.
required_dossiers: Final draft Escritura de Constitución
Passport or corporate identity of the appearing grantor
Power of attorney notarized if Founder is not present
Certified cheque or bank receipt evidencing endowment deposit
Fiscal stamps (papel sellado) purchased at Banco Nacional de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary objects to the deed's wording or stamp deficiencies, cure the defect, replace the fiscal stamps, and execute a corrective notarial addendum without reopening the full formation protocol.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration at the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Fundaciones
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a certified photocopy of the notarized Foundation Deed with the Public Registry, accompanied by the registration application form and official fee payment of approximately US$300. The Registry verifies compliance with Law 25 of 1995, inscribes the foundation in the Registro de Fundaciones, and issues the Certificado de Inscripción (Registration Certificate), thereby granting juridical personality.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarized Escritura de Constitución
Registro Público application form (Solicitud de Inscripción)
Registry fee deposit slip
Copy of the Resident Agent acceptance letter
Power of attorney of the presenting counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon receiving a 'nota de reparo' (written objection), counsel rectifies the deed or submits a written clarification to the Registrar within 10 business days; a re-filing of the corrected deed may be effected administratively without court intervention.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of the Foundation Council and Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (officer annotation) and Resident Agent firm
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, execute the Council appointment certificates naming the initial officers and Resident Agent. File the annotated officer list with the Public Registry for third-party notice. Publish the foundation registration notice in an official gazette if the charter so mandates or if a regulator (e.g., banking institutions) requests evidence.
required_dossiers: Oath or acceptance certificate of each Foundation Council member
Resident agent appointment and acceptance letter
Resolution of the Founder appointing the Council
Certificate de Inscripción from step 3
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer's name is rejected or a missing signature is identified, submit a notarized amendment of appointment with a fresh acceptance letter; the annotation is re-filed and processed as a marginal rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Autoridad de Atención al Contribuyente, DGI, Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Certificado de Inscripción, foundation charter, and Resident Agent identification to DGI to obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) and, if applicable, the Aviso de Operación. The foundation elects territorial-tax treatment: foreign-source income is outside Panamanian tax scope; a non-profit filing status may be asserted where no covered commercial activity occurs in Panamanian territory.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Inscripción of the foundation
Certified copy of the Foundation Charter
RUC application form (Formulario de Registro Único) DGI-RA-01
Resident Agent RUC certificate
Registry of Beneficial Owners filing with UAF (Unidad de Análisis Financiero)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI issues a verification request, respond within 5 business days by submitting certified translations of the charter and updated UAF beneficial ownership attestation; an administrative appeal remains available to the Ministry of Economy and Finance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autoridad Marítima de Panamá (AMP) - Dirección General de Marina Mercante
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Armador y Permiso de Operación de Buque de Transporte de Carga Rodada (Ro-Ro) - Commercial Shipowner License and Ro-Ro Vessel Operation Permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE), Dirección de Seguridad Hídrica y Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I - Registro Ambiental (environmental registration) applicable to international deep-sea shipping operations with no land-based infrastructure; a full EIA (Categoría III) is not required unless the entity acquires or constructs port terminals, ramps, or coastal facilities in Panama.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with MARPOL 73/78 Annexes I, V, and VI: prohibition of oil discharge in Special Areas, no plastic or garbage discharge at sea, maximum fuel sulphur content of 0.50% m/m outside Emission Control Areas, NOx Tier II standards, ballast water management to IMO D-2 standard (Ballast Water Management Convention), and mandatory reporting of waste-oil disposal to MiAMBIENTE and AMP.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: SOLAS fire safety and life-saving appliance certification, ISM Code Safety Management Certificate, Panama-flag statutory hull and load-line inspection clearance, ISPS Code Ship Security Certificate (for international voyage), maritime labor compliance under the Maritime Labour Convention 2006, and STCW crew competency certification verified by AMP Seafarers' Department.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) of the Republic of Panama, operating through the Sede Electrónica e-tax portal at etax.mef.gob.pa. Panama is a unitary state; no sub-national income tax agency exists for central tax collection purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Ensure the Private Interest Foundation (PIF) is validly constituted and recorded: the Pacto Fundacional must be inscribed with the Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público), together with the notarized appointment of officers and the registered resident foundation agent. Step 2: Obtain a Panama digital signature certificate (Firma Electrónica / token) issued by the National Authority for Government Innovation (AIG) for the resident agent or an authorized representative. Step 3: Register the PIF in the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) through the DGI Sede Electrónica, filing the foundation charter, officers resolution, resident agent acceptance, AML/KYC data of founders and beneficiaries, and a physical address or mailing address in Panama. Step 4: If the RoRo vessel is Panamanian-flagged, complete the vessel registration and obtain the Navigation Patent (Patente de Navegación) from the Panama Maritime Authority (AMP); the flat annual navigation tax is paid through AMP, which in turn coordinates with the DGI, so no separate income tax registration is triggered for international shipping profits. Step 5: Activate the ITBMS ledger within the taxpayer account and request DGI authorization of the electronic invoicing series before any Panamanian taxable supply is made. A municipal Aviso de Operación is required only if the PIF maintains a physical commercial establishment in a Panamanian municipality; a purely offshore PIF holding a vessel does not require it.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope — A Panama Private Interest Foundation (Law 25 of 1995) is a separate legal person, not a pass-through vehicle, but the Republic taxes only income sourced within Panamanian territory (Código Fiscal, Artículo 694). Income derived from international ocean RoRo cross-trade, including freight, charter hire, demurrage, and ancillary shipping revenues earned outside Panama, is outside the Panamanian income tax base. A Panamanian-flagged vessel engaged in international voyages is additionally subject to the flat annual navigation tax (Law 8 of 2011), which substitutes for any income tax on the vessel's international operations. The PIF is not located in a statutory tax-exempt zone; its favorable position flows from territorial sourcing, the flat navigation tax regime, and the absence of any Panamanian-source revenue. The PIF remains subject to non-tax registry compliance fees, including the quarterly Tasa Única de Empresas introduced by Law 129 of 2020, to the extent applicable to foundations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a US-style check-the-box election; the tax treatment follows the juridical form of the PIF and the source of income. Material available mechanisms: (1) Flat navigation tax election: a vessel owner may apply the annual per-net-tonnage navigation tax under Law 8 of 2011 in lieu of any territorial income tax attributable to international shipping profits; the election is exercised at AMP registration and evidenced in the DGI annual filing. (2) DGI Tax Residence Certificate: the PIF may apply for an official tax residence certificate through the Sede Electrónica to evidence Panamanian residence for banking, reinsurance, and international administrative purposes. (3) Small-taxpayer simplified ITBMS regime: election available for taxpayers with annual gross receipts at or below the approximate USD 36,000 threshold, subject to current DGI indexation. (4) Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime under Law 41 of 2007 if the foundation later establishes qualifying Panamanian management, which is not activated in this file. (5) There is no domestic hybrid-mismatch election; Panama's territorial system generally eliminates hybrid mismatches with respect to shipping income, and the PIF is not subject to CFC or controlled-foreign-entity rules for its foreign-flag or Panamanian-flag international fleet income.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) — Panamanian banking regulator and national foreign-exchange/financial-information supervisor; Panama has no central bank issuing local fiat. Banco Nacional de Panamá serves as fiscal agent for the State, and Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) operates as the Financial Intelligence Unit for AML/CFT FX-reporting functions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Fully dollarized economy: the U.S. dollar circulates as legal tender alongside the Panamanian Balboa (PAB) pegged at 1:1; capital and current account transactions are fully convertible with no exchange-control law, no approval or declaration requirement for profit remittance, and no restriction on outflow of dividends, interest, royalties, or foundation capital. Balboa paper currency is not issued; only 1:1 coinage is minted, and no central-bank reserve regime constrains cross-border transfers. Treasury exposures in non-USD currencies (CNY, JPY, EUR, KRW) must be cleared offshore or through international banking correspondent rails.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panama imposes no statutory timeline for export-receipt repatriation and no mandatory conversion ratio. RoRo ocean-freight proceeds may remain offshore or be freely cleared into the PIF's Panamanian account without conversion into Balboa and without any FX filing to the SBP. The only binding obligations are the UAF cash-transaction report for amounts above USD 10,000 and general AML/CFT surveillance derived from Law 23 of 2015.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Moderate as a supplementary clearing rail; materially lower as a primary repository. Panama lacks a dedicated EMI license comparable to the EU EMI Directive; SBP regulates fintech activity under Decree Law 2 of 2008 and Law 23 of 2015. Offshore digital EMIs (Airwallex, Brex, Wise Business) are not recognized depository institutions in Panama and generally require a Panamanian licensed bank partner or a foreign banking group license to hold funds; they are therefore unsuitable as the sole corporate account for ISIC 5012 RoRo charter-hire settlements that require full SWIFT MT103 and correspondent-bank capture. Acceptable use is limited to visibility dashboards and low-value disbursement wallets, with funds quarantine in a Tier-1 Panamanian bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Required in practice. Under Acuerdo 1-2021 and Law 23 of 2015, Tier-1 Panamanian banks mandate a physical or video-interview KYC session for private-interest foundations; most banks require at least one in-person appearance of the Founder, an appointed Foundation Council member, or a designated Signatory holding notarized and apostilled Power of Attorney. Remote opening is permitted only if the bank's compliance committee approves enhanced due diligence, video evidence, and apostilled identification; first-injection deposit and escrow activation usually trigger an additional physical verification. For capital escrow arrangements, the Founder and the Council Secretary are commonly required to attend a Panama City branch or the bank's wealth-management office.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity and undisclosed settlor/protector of the PIF under Law 25 of 1995 and FATF-aligned SBP guidance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Our registered agent's UAF-compliant due-diligence file; certified copies of the Acta Fundación and Reglamento; sworn beneficial-ownership declaration by the Foundation Council; counsel legal opinion summarizing Articles 6-10 of Law 25; formation tax clearance from the Registro Público; audited foundation financial statements for the past three years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sufficiency of economic substance: booking RoRo freight revenue through a Panamanian PIF without demonstrated commercial function.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISIC 5012 business plan and charter-party portfolio; technical management, commercial management, and crew-management contracts; vessel registration and ISM/SMC/ISPS certificates issued by the Panama Maritime Authority (ARMA); P&I club insurance certificates; operating expenditure ledger segregated from holding-asset income; statutory letter from a Panamanian CPA confirming territorial-taxation compliance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk source-of-funds: repeated SWIFT inflows from shipowners and charterers without documentary chain-of-payment evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three years of audited financial statements with freight-revenue recognition; voyage charters, bills of lading, and demurrage claims; The Baltic Exchange assessments if used; bank references from the originating banks of major counterparties; Sanctions/PEP-screening reports for all charterers, consignees, and beneficial-cargo owners; expedition of freight-invoice trail through a reputable ship broker.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-nexus red flag: vessels or voyage routes intersecting OFAC, EU, UN, or UAF targeted jurisdictions or designated blocked persons.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive sanctions-compliance policy certification approved by the Foundation Council; automated screening reports from a SBP-vetted sanctions engine on all counterparties and vessel GPS histories; route/voyage compliance attestations for each port call; confirmation that charter-parties contain no Iran, North Korea, Syria, Russia-embargo, or Crimea/CSTO nexus; standby LCs only through non-sanctioned confirming banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual Treasury behavior: funding from independent third parties not named in the foundation charter, creating a risk of undisclosed settlor changes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foundation charter and all charter amendments published at the Registro Público; notarial minutes of the Council approving the injection and provider of funds; contractual donation or contribution agreements; full KYC/CDD packet on the contributing entity; bank-proof of the contributor's regulatory licensing or public listing in its home jurisdiction; UAF/RTS report thresholds met without exception.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound contributions to the PIF must reference the foundation charter terms and pass through a regulated banking entity in the sending jurisdiction. Compliant routing: (a) SWIFT MT103 from the originating bank to the PIF's Panamanian account, with purpose-of-payment field 70/71E stating "Foundation capital contribution — Law 25 de 1995, Art. 10" or, for debt financing, "Shareholder loan value D+1 — PIF funding"; (b) beneficiary legal name must exactly match the PIF registered at the Registro Público de Panamá; (c) funds are received in USD with zero conversion due to full dollarization; (d) for USD 10,001 or above, the receiving bank files an RT (Report of Transactions) to the UAF but no SBP central-bank reporting or FX approval is required; (e) the bank's compliance file must contain certified copies of the foundation charter, registered-agent certificate, the Council resolution accepting the injection, and a counterparty KYC package; (f) no mandatory surrender, conversion, or waiting period applies.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for the RoRo carrier use: SWIFT MT103 for charter-hire disbursements, port-expense payments, bunker suppliers, and technical-management fees; SWIFT MT202 COV for interbank cover where the paying bank and the beneficiary bank pass through New York correspondence; commercial letters of credit issued under UCP600 for shipyard repair, spare-parts procurement, and cabin stores; standby letters of credit for charter-party performance and prompt dispatch guarantees. Intra-Panama peso-free payments clear through the ACH/electronic clearing channel operated via Banco Nacional de Panamá; USD cross-border payments are anchored through the bank's correspondent relationships on Fedwire/CHIPS. All payments require matching instructions against the foundation's Council-approved disbursement matrix and the OFAC/UAF screening workflow.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNY/USD, KRW/USD, JPY/USD, and EUR/USD transacted via international bank dealers with SBP-licensed counterparties
Spot FX trades on EUR, GBP, CAD, and CHF cash flows arising from RoRo charter hire and port disbursements
Cross-currency swaps neutralising JPY, EUR, or KRW financing liabilities on vessel acquisitions
Vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars on long-dated charter receivables denominated in non-USD currencies
CME or ICE-listed FX futures on EUR, JPY, and CNH, executed under the Foundation Council's board-approved derivatives mandate

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% on Panama-source taxable income; 0% on non-Panama-source income under Panama's territorial income tax system and the Private Interest Foundation (PIF) exemption.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: PIF is statutorily exempt from Panama corporate income tax on income arising outside Panama; international deep-sea RoRo shipping income earned outside Panama is therefore effectively taxed at 0%; optional Panamanian tonnage-tax regime may apply to the vessel, replacing income tax for shipping operations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 101 (Declaración Anual de Rentas de Personas Jurídicas) filed electronically through the DGI's T@X / e-Tax platform.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within three calendar months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year taxpayer (31 December), the deadline is 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC/NIF, legal name, fiscal year-end, registered agent, and activity code (ISIC 5012).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the PIF foundation license number, resident agent details, and 'Ocean RoRo Vehicle Carrier' as the main activity; foreign beneficial owners are not listed on the face of this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Panama-source income derived from shipping, chartering, or incidental activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude all foreign-source international voyage and charter income; if the PIF has only foreign-source operations, enter zero and attach a brief statement that all income is non-Panamanian-source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct deductions and allocable costs specifically attributable to Panama-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not deduct expenses against foreign-source income on this form; maintain separate schedules for vessel operating costs, crew costs, and charter expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panama-source gross revenue minus allowed deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a purely offshore PIF, net taxable income is zero; for any Panama-source shipping services, apply the normal territorial calculation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 25% corporate rate to net taxable income, less prepayments and withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If net taxable income is zero, enter zero; if the PIF uses the tonnage-tax election, report the tonnage tax amount in the appropriate supplementary schedule instead of the 25% rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final amount of tax due or overpayment to be credited.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If all income is foreign-source, the final balance is zero; any prior monthly prepayments for Panama-source tax may be claimed as credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing fines range from USD 50 to USD 5,000; late payment triggers a 10% surcharge plus monthly interest (approximately 1.25% per month or fraction thereof); persistent non-filing may lead to presumptive assessment and loss of good-standing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on distributions made from profits that have been subject to Panamanian corporate income tax; 15.5% on distributions from profits that have not been taxed in Panama, such as foreign-source shipping income of the PIF.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficiary or shareholder must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC / Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) from the competent authority of the treaty jurisdiction, provide evidence of beneficial ownership, and submit a written Treaty Relief Request to the Panamanian withholding agent before payment. The withholding agent must file the supporting documentation with the DGI and apply the reduced treaty rate only after DGI acknowledgement or as otherwise provided in the relevant double-taxation agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid for use of IP in Panama: statutory 15% withholding (treaty rates generally 5%-10%); interest paid to non-residents on Panamanian-source debt obligations: statutory 6% withholding (treaty rates generally 5%-10%). For a PIF with foreign-source international shipping operations, these withholdings are generally not triggered because the related income is not sourced in Panama.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/. 5,000,000 (Panamanian balboas / USD equivalent) in gross annual revenue, combined with related-party transactions exceeding B/. 1,000,000, triggers mandatory Local File and Master File documentation.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Law 254 of 2019 and implementing decrees apply Economic Substance Requirements (ESR) to entities engaged in Relevant Activities, including shipping, pure equity holding, IP holding, and distribution and service centers. A PIF operating an international RoRo vessel must maintain a real and adequate presence in Panama by demonstrating local management, employees, physical premises, and core income-generating activities conducted in or from Panama, and must file the annual economic substance declaration with the DGI.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of Panama-source income, use of false invoices, overstatement of deductions, or concealing the PIF's actual Panamanian shipping activity behind the foreign-income exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud penalties under Panama's fiscal and penal laws: fines of USD 50,000 to USD 500,000 and imprisonment from 2 to 5 years; civil liability for the undeclared tax plus a 10% surcharge and monthly interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, foundation council members, and the registered agent may be criminally prosecuted, subjected to travel bans and asset freezes, and held jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of evaded taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare and file mandatory Local File / Master File documentation, or entering into related-party charter, management, or financing transactions that deviate from the arm's length standard to shift profits offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI transfer pricing adjustments resulting in additional 25% corporate income tax plus a 10% surcharge; fines for missing documentation range from USD 10,000 to USD 50,000; intentional false documentation may attract criminal penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign or approve false TP returns can be held personally liable for underpaid taxes and may face criminal sanctions where the documentary falsehood constitutes tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Failure of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF as a letterbox entity that files zero returns, holds a Panamanian vessel registration, and conducts all management, crew, and commercial operations abroad without any real economic presence in Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Economic substance fines of USD 10,000 to USD 100,000 per fiscal year for non-compliance or false substance declarations; possible deregistration of the foundation and loss of the Panamanian flag/vessel registry privileges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members and the resident agent may be disqualified, fined, and barred from serving as registered agents; directors willfully filing false substance declarations are exposed to criminal liability for false documentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF to conceal the beneficial ownership of vessel charter proceeds, laundering funds through non-compliant payment rails, facilitating sanctioned-party trade, or deliberately rejecting know-your-customer and source-of-funds verification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Panama's AML regime (Law 23 of 2015 and Penal Code provisions), penalties include imprisonment from 5 to 12 years, fines up to USD 5 million, asset confiscation, and administrative fines up to double the value of the illicit transaction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, trustees, and ultimate beneficial owners face personal criminal indictment, asset freezing, international travel bans, extradition, and civil confiscation; the corporate veil of the PIF is pierced when it is used as an instrument of illicit conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Payment of Annual PIF Fee and Registry Abuses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to pay the annual government fee, failure to maintain a licensed resident agent in Panama, or knowingly certifying false good-standing to banks, ship registries, or counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Suspension and eventual cancellation of the foundation's legal personality; financial penalties up to USD 10,000 plus the accumulated annual fees; loan and banking facilities are immediately jeopardized.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The resident agent is answerable to the DGI and Superintendency of Banks; foundation council members can be held liable for civil restitution to third parties for injuries caused by the false certification.
